module.purpose: Stores and manages Query instances in the query core, providing build/add/remove/find and event notifications.
module.summary: QueryCache is a Subscribable container that holds a map of Query objects keyed by queryHash. It constructs queries via build, adds/removes them, clears all, and supports lookup by hash or filter matching. It emits typed notification events to listeners and batches notifications through notifyManager. It also propagates focus/online signals to all queries.
module.businessContext: Data fetching/caching library core. If it fails, queries are not cached, deduplicated, or updated correctly, breaking client UI consistency.
classes: QueryCache (~L92-223): Manages collection of Query instances with subscriber notifications

detail.name: build
detail.signature:
build<
    TQueryFnData = unknown,
    TError = DefaultError,
    TData = TQueryFnData,
    TQueryKey extends QueryKey = QueryKey,
  >(
    client: QueryClient,
    options: WithRequired<
      QueryOptions<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey>,
      'queryKey'
    >,
    state?: QueryState<TData, TError>,
  ): Query<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey>
postconditions: Returns a Query instance matching the resolved queryHash
If no matching Query existed, a new Query is constructed with client.defaultQueryOptions(options), client.getQueryDefaults(queryKey), and optional state, and registered via this.add
invariants: queryHash is either options.queryHash or hashQueryKeyByOptions(queryKey, options)
edgeCases: options.queryHash provided: used directly, skipping hash computation
Existing query for queryHash: returned without new Query creation or add call
No existing query: new Query created with default options from client and added to cache
stateMutations: Adds a new Query to the cache via this.add when none exists for the hash
detail.summary: Returns an existing Query for the given hash if present in the cache, otherwise creates a new Query from client and options, adds it to the cache, and returns it.

specTests.then: returns a new Query whose queryHash equals hashQueryKeyByOptions(['k'], options) and cache contains that Query
returns the existing Query without calling new Query or this.add

units.name: add

detail.name: add
detail.signature: add(query: Query<any, any, any, any>): void
preconditions: query is a Query instance with a queryHash property
postconditions: If query.queryHash is not already a key, query is stored in this.#queries under that key
If stored, this.notify is called with { type: 'added', query }
If query.queryHash already exists, no mutation or notification occurs
invariants: Each queryHash maps to at most one query
Cache only grows via addition of new hashes
edgeCases: Duplicate queryHash: method is no-op and emits no notification
First insertion of a hash: stores and notifies
stateMutations: this.#queries: adds mapping from query.queryHash to query when absent
detail.summary: Adds a query to the internal cache keyed by its queryHash if not already present, and notifies observers with an 'added' event.

specLiterals.role: Literal type field in notification object emitted when a query is added

specTests.then: this.#queries has key 'h1' with query and notify called with { type: 'added', query }
Cache unchanged and notify not called

units.name: remove

detail.name: remove
detail.signature: remove(query: Query<any, any, any, any>): void
preconditions: The query argument must be a valid Query object with a queryHash property.
The QueryCache instance must be initialized with a #queries Map.
postconditions: If the query exists in the cache, it is destroyed.
If the query reference matches the one stored in the cache, it is removed from the #queries Map.
A notification of type 'removed' is emitted if the query was present in the cache.
invariants: The #queries Map remains consistent: a query is only deleted if its reference matches the stored instance.
edgeCases: If the query is not found in the cache, no action is taken and no notification is emitted.
If the query exists in the cache but is a different reference than the one passed in, destroy() is called but the cache entry is not deleted.
If the query is null or undefined, this.#queries.get will not find it and the method exits early.
stateMutations: query.destroy() (invokes cleanup on the query object)
detail.summary: Removes a query from the cache, destroying it and notifying observers if it exists.

specLiterals.role: Notification type identifying that a query was removed from the cache.

detail.name: clear
postconditions: All queries returned by getAll() have been removed from the cache
edgeCases: When the cache is empty, getAll() returns an empty array and forEach does nothing, making clear() a no-op
stateMutations: Removes all queries from the internal cache storage
detail.summary: Clears all cached queries by removing each one within a single batched notification context.

specTests.then: All queries are removed from the cache and notifications are batched
The method completes without error as a no-op

detail.name: find
detail.signature: find<TQueryFnData = unknown, TError = DefaultError, TData = TQueryFnData>(filters: WithRequired<QueryFilters, 'queryKey'>): Query<TQueryFnData, TError, TData> | undefined
preconditions: filters.queryKey must be provided (enforced by WithRequired<QueryFilters, 'queryKey'>)
postconditions: Returns the first Query from getAll() that satisfies matchQuery with the defaulted filters, or undefined if none match
invariants: exact defaults to true unless explicitly overridden by a property in filters
edgeCases: No matching query exists: returns undefined
Multiple queries match: returns the first one encountered in getAll() order
filters explicitly sets exact: false: the override takes precedence over the default true
filters omits exact: exact defaults to true
detail.summary: Finds the first cached Query matching the given filters, defaulting exact key matching to true, and returns undefined when no match exists.

specLiterals.role: Default value for the exact matching flag in filter resolution; filters can override it via spread

specTests.when: find is called with filters { queryKey: ['user', 1] }
find is called with filters { queryKey: ['nonexistent'] }

units.name: findAll

detail.name: findAll
postconditions: If filters object has no keys, returns all queries from the cache.
If filters object has keys, returns only queries for which matchQuery(filters, query) returns true.
edgeCases: Default parameter filters={} results in unfiltered list.
Non-empty filters object triggers filtering using matchQuery.
detail.summary: Returns all queries in the cache, optionally filtered by the provided QueryFilters. When no filters are supplied, returns the complete list of queries; otherwise returns only those queries that match the filters via matchQuery.

specTests.then: returns array containing both Q1 and Q2
returns array containing only queries for which matchQuery(filters, query) is true

units.name: notify

detail.name: notify
preconditions: this.listeners is an array of listener functions
notifyManager.batch is a function that accepts a callback
postconditions: All current listeners have been invoked exactly once with the provided event
All listener calls occur within the notifyManager.batch callback
invariants: this.listeners is not modified by this method
notifyManager.batch is called exactly once per notify invocation
edgeCases: If this.listeners is empty, batch callback executes with no listener calls
If a listener throws, the error propagates out of notifyManager.batch and stops further listeners in the forEach

raises: Any exception thrown by a listener is re-thrown by notifyManager.batch

detail.summary: Dispatches a query cache notification event to all registered listeners, wrapping listener invocations in a notifyManager.batch call to coalesce updates.

specTests.when: notify(event) is called with a valid event
specTests.then: l1 and l2 are each called exactly once with event, and both calls happen inside the batch callback

detail.name: onFocus
postconditions: All queries returned by this.getAll() have had their onFocus method called exactly once
All calls are wrapped inside a single notifyManager.batch execution
edgeCases: When cache contains zero queries, notifyManager.batch is still called with an empty forEach loop and no query.onFocus invocations occur
detail.summary: Invokes onFocus on every cached query within a batched notification, signaling that the application regained focus.

specTests.then: notifyManager.batch is invoked once, and both q1.onFocus and q2.onFocus are called exactly once inside the batch

detail.name: onOnline
postconditions: All queries returned by this.getAll() have had their onOnline() method called
The calls are wrapped in a notifyManager.batch execution
edgeCases: When the cache contains no queries, the forEach loop does nothing and no error is thrown
stateMutations: May mutate individual Query states via query.onOnline() calls
detail.summary: Notifies all cached queries that the application is online by invoking each query's onOnline method within a batched notification context.

specTests.then: notifyManager.batch is invoked and both q1.onOnline() and q2.onOnline() are executed exactly once
